provider_scope: matched source-backed PPTX lifecycle through explicit bytes, warm recently-written file, or caller-owned bounded range adapter
timing_scope: open, plan, and publication durations contain only their immediately surrounding public API calls; setup, source construction, reservations, diagnostics, drops, and correctness checks are outside the clocks
allocation_scope: optional operation-scoped global-system-allocator counters; four non-nested regions surround only the existing source-open, destination-open, planning, and publication timers, while diagnostics, correctness checks, report construction, and serialization remain outside
allocation_open_source_scope: source presentation open allocation region begins immediately before the source-open timer and finishes immediately after it; source-open correctness checks and cache diagnostics are outside
allocation_open_destination_scope: destination editor open allocation region begins immediately before the destination-open timer and finishes immediately after it; destination-open correctness checks and cache diagnostics are outside
allocation_plan_scope: cross-slide planning allocation region begins immediately before the planning timer and finishes immediately after it; plan metadata checks and cache diagnostics are outside
allocation_publication_scope: cross-slide publication allocation region begins immediately before the publication timer and finishes immediately after it; output checks, cache diagnostics, and drops are outside
range_scope: PptxRangeSource logical adapter counters; request lengths and returned bytes describe caller-visible ReadAt calls, not physical network or filesystem I/O
file_scope: fresh task-owned files are staged once before warmups and reopened through FileSource for every iteration; files are recently written and warm-cache, with no cold-cache claim
rss_scope: optional process-wide VmRSS/VmHWM snapshots from procfs; setup and unrelated process memory remain in scope and no comparative RSS claim is authorized
